title: CardZone Loadout Loop rules test cases (cz04)
generated_for: cz07 loadout_rules.gd headless tests (GUT or the project's test runner)

conventions.seats: P1 is the first player, P2 the second (D8). A round is P1's turn, then P2's.
conventions.cards: Cards are named by code (see `cards`). A weapon with tucked attachments is written WEAPON+ATT(+ATT) and is one card (D2). Lists are in order: loadout top→bottom, hand in hand order, line left→right (D7).
conventions.held: setup.players.X.held = how many cards at the top of the loadout are held cards (face-down, hidden from the opponent unless held_cards_public).
conventions.areas: Area ids match data/areas: docks(1), farmstead(2), quarry(3), radio_hill(4), motel(5), rail_yard(6), old_town (the Core). Distance: same 0, ring neighbours or old_town 1, else 2.
conventions.data_ids: Card codes map to CardDB ids through cards.<code>.data_id (e.g. HRF = hunting_rifle, CZ-016). Balance keys match data/balance.tres one for one; packing_rule and adrenaline_mode are written as their names (hold_and_stow | rack_swap, move_or_search | move_only) and map to the data_enums values.
conventions.round: zone_card = the number of the last Zone card flipped; it equals the round. gas and drops are the state after that card.
conventions.fixtures: Setups are fixtures: build them with MatchState.from_fixture (RQ-11). They need not be reachable from a real match start, except the new_match cases.
conventions.actions: Player actions per U1: play(card, adrenaline), move(to), loot(source: pile code | 'drop:CODE' | 'crate:CODE'), shoot(weapon, target), frag(area), attach(attachment, weapon), patch_up, ditch(card), end_turn(hold | rack_move{from,to}), brace(cards in order), undo, concede; setup action drop(area) (RQ-04). Test hooks: auto_draw, check, view(seat).
conventions.card_refs: An action naming a code acts on the first matching copy: hand order (play, ditch, hold), line order (shoot, attach), next-hand order (brace). See RQ-07.
conventions.automatic: end_turn runs the gas check, Pack, then the next seat's draw; after P2's end_turn it runs the hard-end check or the round start (Bounty, Zone flip, gas, drop, final circle) and P1's draw.
conventions.expect: Each step's expect lists only the fields that matter; compare those and ignore the rest. legal:false means the engine must reject the action and leave the state unchanged. Player fields: area, health, loadout, hand, line, move, search, down, next_draw, eliminated, held_count, nonhit_count. 'shot' is the last shot or Frag result: damage_before_brace, cover, down, hits, braced, bounty_heal; a Frag gives frag.{seat}.{...}. pending_brace is the seat that must brace next (null if none). match_end is {result: win|draw, winner, cause: shot|frag|gas|final_circle|hard_end|concede}. crate is a list of {owner, area, cards, free_picks}. removed lists cards removed from the game face up (ditched, Spent), in order. action_count counts logged actions since the fixture. view is a subset of view(seat); view_absent lists paths that must not exist; view_equal_b means view(seat) on setup_b (after the same actions) must be identical (P18).
conventions.switches: Tunable overrides are in setup.balance; everything else is balance_defaults.

rules_questions.question: Is there a Brace step when the defender has no card that can brace?
rules_questions.context: R24 says there is no Brace step at damage 0, and R27 removes it for a Suppressor. Nothing says what happens when the damage is above 0 but the defender's next hand has no Brace card left (none printed, or all already braced this turn, R26). If the engine skips the prompt, the shooter learns something private about the next hand (P1, P18), and in hot-seat the speed of the reply gives it away.
rules_questions.proposed_answer: Whenever damage before Brace is above 0 and there is no Suppressor, the engine always waits for a `brace` action, which may be empty. The UI may auto-send an empty Brace for a human defender with nothing to pick, after a short fixed delay. The AI always sends one. Every `brace("")` step in these cases assumes this.
rules_questions.status: open - proposed answer assumed by dependent cases

rules_questions.question: Does the held count (P3) drop when a held card braces?
rules_questions.context: P3 shows how many cards the opponent held. R25 sends a braced card to the bottom and P11 reveals it, so a braced held card is no longer on top and is no longer secret.
rules_questions.proposed_answer: Yes. The held count is the number of held cards still on top of the loadout. A braced held card loses its held mark. The mark also clears when the card is drawn.
rules_questions.status: open - proposed answer assumed by dependent cases

rules_questions.question: Does a thrown Frag pass through the line?
rules_questions.context: U1 lists `frag(area)` as 'playing a Frag', and R6 says a play moves the card to the line. R20 says a Frag is Spent after it resolves.
rules_questions.proposed_answer: No. The Frag goes from the hand straight out of the game (face up, P12). It never sits in the line, so it never changes line order or the stow. `play(FRG)` is illegal: a Frag is used only through `frag(area)`.
rules_questions.status: open - proposed answer assumed by dependent cases

rules_questions.question: How is the drop recorded?
rules_questions.context: S5 sets the drop order (P2, then P1, outer areas only), but U1's action list has no drop action. Replay needs it (§13: setup plus action list).
rules_questions.proposed_answer: Add `drop(area)` as a setup action for each seat, logged in the action list before round 1. P2 drops first, then P1. Only areas 1–6 are allowed. Round 1 starts automatically after P1's drop. It can't be undone.
rules_questions.status: open - proposed answer assumed by dependent cases

rules_questions.question: Does a shot that deals 0 use the weapon's shot?
rules_questions.context: R24 says a 0-damage shot has no Brace step. R12 counts shots at declare.
rules_questions.proposed_answer: Yes. Declaring the shot uses one of the weapon's shots and commits the turn (U3), even when it deals 0. The shot preview (P19) shows the 0 first, so the player isn't surprised.
rules_questions.status: open - proposed answer assumed by dependent cases

rules_questions.question: Can a thrower who is eliminated by their own Frag claim the Bounty?
rules_questions.context: R34 has the Hits land, then the Bounty claim, then eliminations. R37 says an eliminated shooter doesn't claim, and R45 says elimination happens when a Hit must be taken from an empty stack, which is during the landing step. If the claim came first, its heal could put a Hit back on a stack that is about to be needed.
rules_questions.proposed_answer: No. The landing step decides who is eliminated (R45). A thrower eliminated there doesn't claim, and R47 or R45 ends the match. The claim's heal never saves a player who is already out.
rules_questions.status: open - proposed answer assumed by dependent cases

rules_questions.question: Which copy does an action name?
rules_questions.context: The cases name cards by code (`play SCV`). A hand or next hand can hold two identical copies. For rules purposes copies are the same, but replay and the held marks need instance ids.
rules_questions.proposed_answer: The engine's actions carry card instance ids. When a case names a code, the runner resolves it to the first matching copy: hand order for play/ditch/hold, line order for shoot/attach, next-hand order for brace. A weapon is named by its code alone or by its code plus attachments (`HRF+RDS`).
rules_questions.status: open - proposed answer assumed by dependent cases

rules_questions.question: Should the engine pair hand 4 with drop cost 3?
rules_questions.context: §16.4a says that when the dev panel switches `hand_size` to 4, `supply_drop_cost` should be 3.
rules_questions.proposed_answer: The pairing belongs to the dev panel (cz13) only. The engine reads every key on its own and never changes one because of another. The hand-4 cases set both keys, as the panel would. None of their results depends on the drop cost.
rules_questions.status: open - proposed answer assumed by dependent cases

rules_questions.question: What if `final_circle_hits` is empty?
rules_questions.context: R43 repeats the last value when the list is shorter than 3, but an empty list has no last value.
rules_questions.proposed_answer: BalanceConfig rejects an empty list, or any negative value, at load (cz05, fail loudly). No case is needed in the rules engine.
rules_questions.status: open - proposed answer assumed by dependent cases

rules_questions.question: Field names of `view(state, seat)`
rules_questions.context: §16.2 says what each seat sees but doesn't name the fields. The fairness test (P18) compares whole views, so every field has to be either always public or always derived from public data.
rules_questions.proposed_answer: Proposed names, used by the view cases: `opponent.{area, health, line, fired, held_count, held_cards (only if held_cards_public), next_draw_hits and hand_hits (only if hits_on_top_public), loadout_count (only if loadout_count_public), down, hand_count, eliminated}`, plus `me` (the seat's own full state), the public table state, and during a Brace either `shot_preview {damage, may_brace}` (the shooter) or `brace_prompt {damage, next_hand}` (the defender). A hidden field is left out entirely, never sent as null. cz07 may rename the fields; the runner then maps them.
rules_questions.status: open - proposed answer assumed by dependent cases

rules_questions.question: Fixtures and test hooks
rules_questions.context: Most cases start mid-turn from a state that is legal but wasn't reached by playing (for example a hand with a looted Plate Vest in round 5). Some setups also break the totals: health plus Hits in loadout, hand and line always comes to `health`, but a few fixtures shrink a loadout to isolate a rule (short loadouts, an empty loadout for Pull).
rules_questions.proposed_answer: cz07 provides `MatchState.from_fixture(setup)`, which accepts the setup block as written (pools, fired counts, held marks, looted-this-turn, drops and drop rounds, crates), plus three test hooks: `auto_draw` (the active seat's start-of-turn draw), `check` (no action, compare only), and `view(seat)`. `end_turn` runs everything automatic up to the next decision: gas check, Pack, the next draw, and the round start (Bounty, Zone flip, final circle).
rules_questions.status: open - proposed answer assumed by dependent cases

cases.why: No pool: illegal. Rail Yard to Quarry is distance 2: illegal in one step. Via the Core it takes 2 Move.

cases.why: Search 3 < 4. Pump Shotgun is a Quarry pile. Long Scope costs 3 but its pile is empty.

cases.why: Pump Shotgun DMG 3, same area (no Cover), P2 not Down. P2 chooses not to brace: 3 Hits on top.

cases.title: Attach: free, permanent, the pair is one card; Red-dot +1 DMG

cases.title: Attach limits: 2 per weapon, different names; a loose attachment plays for nothing
cases.why: A third attachment and a second Red-dot are illegal. The spare Red-dot is a loose card: play it to the line with no effect.

cases.why: Rail Yard to Farmstead is distance 2. Hunting Rifle RNG 1 + 1 = 2 reaches; Farmstead Cover 1. (A scope on a RNG-2 gun has no effect: max RNG 2.)
